utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. We are still on cross-examination. Can we have the witness? (Witness enters court) (Interpreter enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Remind the witness that he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (in interpretation): Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, you can continue your cross-examination. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Good morning, your Honours. Thank you. Good morning, Mr. Moerbauer. Mr. Moerbauer, yesterday before we adjourned you answered that the things that you received or reviewed were never listed by you officially, nor was Mr. Delalic present when making such a list, as we know that he was arrested in Munich, nor was his defence counsel or any other authorised representative present. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I would object to this way of wording, because there was a moment when he listed and described everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The question was at the time he did this list the defendant was not there and his counsel wasn't there. That is the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: That's okay. All right. So explained it's good for us. Thank you. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. Moerbauer, did you put some kind of a mark on each paper that you held by which you could recognise that paper wherever you were to see it or at some other time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Each paper that was translated and that was deemed relevant to the case was referenced. I put a sticker on it with the relevant number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, your last report on the review of documentation was compiled by you on 22nd April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So far as I can recall, that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This entire material, together with a letter, was handed over to the court on 30th April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As regards the specific date when it went to the court, I'm not familiar with it, because we have a department within the police headquarters that deals with that matter, and they are the police would transfer it, but when it comes to the search and the arrest warrants and the documents relevant thereto, they were provided earlier to the court. So this had to do with the objects that were seized and in regard to which the reports were drawn up, that is to say the videotapes and the documents, and the court received those reports at the end of the month of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In addition to those reports in which you conveyed some of your views and knowledge regarding the objects you had reviewed and which allegedly originate from the places which were searched, did you hand over any other specification of the documents which would list each document, its name, place and time, where it was found or seized or, rather, the place and time when you seized it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now in the interim an interim report was prepared. That was in mid-April, early April. That was sent to the court. That concerned a document that contained a judgment by a Bosnian military court. Now with regard to the documents that said they were referenced and on the basis of the index of the analysis report --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I ask you, Mr. Moerbauer, could you please answer my question? In addition to those reports contained in the file and which serve to refresh your memory, did you draw up any kind of special list containing just the names of the documents and the way in which you gained possession of those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now in drawing up the reports with the analysis the judge could determine where the objects had been seized and to know where the videotapes and the relevant documents came from. So that was made clear in the reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, did every page have an index number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only the relevant documents that were also translated. They were given a number. Documents that were not deemed relevant were not referenced and also that was the case of ID papers. They weren't given any reference. In the various files there were on occasion copies of documents that were also in other files. So we didn't reference those in addition or translate them a second time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. The indexing was done after you started viewing the documents, that is 20th March.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's an error in the transcript, which I think may affect things and I would like to point it out. It's page 4, line 22. The answer says: "Now in drawing". I think what he said was: "No. In drawing ..." I think his answer was "No".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a report of 22nd April 1996 regarding the search, Koppstrasse 14 and Mucic Zdravko. It says analysis. That is a report. I1-12, that relates to files, folders with documents, Zdravko Mucic and Inda-Bau. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. Moerbauer --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Excuse me. May I interrupt for a moment about the assertion done by Mr. Ackerman? There is the possibility that something confusing might be a reason you might ask again the question and clarify that point, which is not clear to me, because the transcript is not right on the video, the part Mr. Ackerman was pointing out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The answer to my question has not yet come. You started indexing the documents after 20th March. That's when you started viewing them, or was it earlier? MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I apologise. The witness said yesterday that he started to work with the interpreter on the 22nd, a Friday, to review the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: 22nd March. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): And then he indexed each he reviewed. That was the witness's answer yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The videotapes that were seized at Zdravko Mucic were indexed on the same day by colleague Panzer and they were given as references M1A through D. Now the tapes from Inda-Bau and Taubergasse 15/14, the ones coming from there, they were indexed starting on the following day. Now the folders, the documents seized from Inda-Bau, were indexed on 18th -- that is the same day -- in the course of copying. They were given the letter "I" and the individual documents that were in the folders were given, starting from 22nd March, the individual documents, as I gave them to the interpreter, were given a further number. Say it comes out of the first folder, that would be I1. Then the first document in that folder would get another number, number 1. So that document would bear the reference I1/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, to make it clear to all of us, you said that as of the following day Mr. Panzer undertook to identify the videotapes which were allegedly taken from Mr. Delalic's apartment and from the Inda-Bau company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this kind of binder had the index "I" without an indication how many documents it contained and which documents it contained before you started to review it together with an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The folders were given the initial letter "I" the same day. I said depending where they come from, talking about Taubergasse 15/14, that was given "D". That happened on the same day without the interpreter. The individual documents were not referenced that same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Within these folders, for instance folder I1, did you individually index the papers in the period from 22nd March to 2nd April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would hand an individual document to the interpreter, and at that point in time it was given the reference number. So it was as and when these documents were translated to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the numbers placed on the documents remain there permanently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were transferred to the court with those reference numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, the videotapes, you can recognise them only by the indication I or D attached to them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you know that that indication regarding the tapes from Inda-Bau and Zejnil Delalic, that that number was placed there by your colleague, Panzer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to these videotapes and this system of referencing, you also know that Mr. Panzer was not the person who carried out the search in Inda-Bau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Navrat, who was the person doing the research, brought the videotapes in an open box to room 133 and handed them over to you -- 331, sorry -- Room 331?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Panzer spent more time that same day preparing -- working on the statement of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Panzer at the time Mucic was being questioned was present in the room.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Navrat did not give any objects to Mr. Panzer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Navrat gave all the objects -- brought all the objects found allegedly in Inda-Bau in an open cardboard box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Moerbauer, that on that day in Room 331 you did not at any point in time seal this open box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The box, it was not taped closed, but it was a cardboard box that had a top. So it was closed. Flaps were intertwined, as it were, and it was indicated where the objects came from?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there is no doubt that each one of you or anybody else, if necessary, could have opened the lid of the box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the box would have been easy to open.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said, so would you please confirm if I understood you well, that Mr. Panzer, who did not participate in the search of Inda-Bau, established a surplus of three tapes in this box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In analysing the video cassettes we ascertained that there were more video cassettes, and when it comes to the video cassettes seized, Taubergasse 15/14, that error was noted by my colleagues, by the colleagues who carried out the search, and that mistake was corrected, reported, shall we say, on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this error from Inda-Bau was established by Mr. Panzer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who discovered the error I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it is not correct? Yesterday you did not tell the truth when you confirmed that this error was confirmed by Mr. Panzer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The error was notified via a report by Mr. Panzer. Now, as to whether in the interim there were notes entered into the record is something I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, you cannot say even today the exact names of the videotapes that appeared additionally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, the number of videos was consistent with that given to the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but you did not answer my question. Even today in this court you are unable to indicate the names of the videotapes which appeared additionally in between the record made on the spot and the report that you yourself compiled later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as the Taubergasse 15, Door 14 goes, 28 videotapes were seized there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Inda-Bau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Inda-Bau 51 according to the record were found there and, in fact, we found that there were really 54 videos there. Now in the original record we didn't refer to the individual videotapes by name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you cannot give us the name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How can you give the name? His position was originally in the box there were 54, although they were counted as 51. So how can he separate those possibly? MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I can simply say that he cannot tell us the names, but it is up to the witness to answer the questions. Thank you, your Honours for helping me. Mr. Moerbauer, I should like to ask you, if you can, to tell me is it true that in your record of 22nd April 1996 and which as a part of your memory is found in folder 1, which you tried to identify yesterday, in that report under point D1 -- D5, is it stated that this is a binder called binder of receipts with the names and amounts of donations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you referring to the report of 22nd April 1996 regarding Taubergasse 15, Door 14; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, under the index D5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says here a red ledger with names and amounts listed. As far as I can recall, these were donations that went to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it also indicated under D6 that there was an indoor football tournament. I'm referring to the same report. I'm just asking you to remind yourself. I'm not asking you to identify it. I'm just asking you whether there is a reference to an indoor football tournament?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar that in the same report D23 was an evening of folk songs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that some videotapes did have a football tournament on them. That was the annual tournament in Vienna, I remember that there were some demonstrations on videos and, in fact, those things were on some of the tapes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, did you also view the cassettes where there are some feature films?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The tapes where there were feature films were viewed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also with broadcasts that are comedy programmes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's right, but one might add that sometimes there's footage of television programmes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've answered my question. All such videotapes which I only mentioned by way of example, did you list all these videotapes and turn them over to the State Prosecutor of Austria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The list of the videotapes was sent to the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a separate list of these videotapes, such as I have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No separate list was drawn up in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you return the video cassette that had nothing to do with what the court order called for? Did you return such video cassettes either to their owner or to his authorised representative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The objects had been seized on the basis of a court warrant and so as far as the seized objects go, they can only be handed over by the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, I am here asking the questions and you are here to respond, so we're not conducting a discussion here, but in the court order it states -- it says that only the tapes referring to the torture of prisoners and war crimes in BH are pertinent ones, and you will agree with me that the ones that contain folk songs are not relevant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The videotapes which I seized in the apartment of Zdravko Mucic contained this. All of the other videotapes that were seized --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Residovic. I would like you to let the witness finish his answer before interrupting him, please. Thank you. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. Turone, please, I would like not to be interrupted and as for Mr. Zdravko Mucic, he has his own counsel, and they will ask the relevant questions in that regard. May I proceed, your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you. Mr. Moerbauer out of 100 pieces of paper, documents that you seized from the Inda-Bau company premises, through your memory and your notes you pointed to the documents that you had in your possession between 22nd March and 2nd April. Please can you tell me how many documents were contained in I1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As regards the exact number, I'm afraid I can't tell you that. The list of the documents that were translated is stated in the analysis report, but actually there were considerably more documents in there than that, because some of them were not translated, and some of them were not deemed relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, if we could just repeat something that you had said yesterday, you do not speak Serbo-Croatian or Croatian-Serbian or, as it is called today Croatian/Serbian-Bosnian language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the language that a certain document was written, you are unable to recognise it on that basis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but we're talking also about documents in German.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. You've answered the question. Mr. Moerbauer, you can only determine the -- you can only recognise the documents that have been written in German language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to the contents of the documents, I can read the documents in German and I can compare with the German documents. You can see on the basis of the analysis report what the contents of the documents was. Yes, that I can determine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, during your training you had no special education in graphology; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not given that kind of training.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you cannot recognise the handwriting of a certain individual based on your expert knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At no time during your analysis did you submit the documents to the graphologic test, in other words documents that were in certain individuals' handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never proceeded to analysis and did not ask for any graphological analysis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At no time did you ask for a graphological analysis of the signatures of the documents that you were analysing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just said that no analysis was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Moerbauer, you testified before this Trial Chamber that the letter that was written allegedly by Mr. Zejnil Delalic was indeed written by him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't know which letter you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: By recognising certain documents that you allegedly analysed, you yesterday stated that it was a letter that Mr. Delalic sent, for instance, to another person; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you mean the letter that begins: "Dear Edina", now that document, that stems from folder D4. I can tell you that much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you do not know who wrote this letter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, that letter was signed "Z Delalic" or "Zejnil Delalic".

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally cannot testify, based on your knowledge, that is lack of graphological knowledge, who the author of this letter is?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. Nobody needs particular to be a handwriting expert to make some conclusions on handwriting anyway. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But what is the basis for saying that this letter is written by Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I was saying something about the signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Does he know the signatures? How can he say that? All he can say is that this letter was found among the folders. He doesn't know who wrote that letter and whether that letter bears really the signatures of Delalic. How can he say that? All he can say is that the letter was found. It's in a language which he doesn't understand and cannot read.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is a language he doesn't understand and he cannot read. He has not seen Delalic writing letters. All he can say is this letter was found in the folder and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, he said this was a letter which appeared to come from Delalic. This is what -- probably he cannot say anything more about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: All that he can say is this letter was found in the folder, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: In any event, I'm not sure you are proving letters now. You are not proving any letters, whether anything was written or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: She's challenging the report of the officer that this letter was written by Delalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, you carry on with your questions. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honour, I contest that this witness can recognise anything. I am going to submit a file. It is a file, folder that the witness had yesterday with him. I don't know what number it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: None of the documents is in evidence. None of them is in evidence. I don't know what you are arguing about, because there's no need. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I would like to request that the witness take another look at the documents which he identified yesterday. If this is not the proper way to do it, I will request that the witness be shown this document by way of the usher, and the document can also be shown to the Prosecution. (Handed to Prosecution). (Handed to witness). No identification is needed. Can this document please just be shown to the witness, so that he can recognise it if he can?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. I will ask the question, please. So if you can just please answer my question. Number 004731083 is not the number that you put there while you reviewed this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this document is written in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this document was not submitted to a graphological analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Moerbauer, that on this piece of paper there is not a single mark that was put there in your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this piece of paper in no way -- that you cannot recognise this document as your own in any way if you only look at this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can recall that this document was among the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, this document contains no mark of any place or time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There are no markings on this document about the chain of custody between your colleague Navrat and yourself. Is there such a marking there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. May I kindly ask the question to be repeated, because my client wanted to give an answer before him, so I did not quite hear all the translation into English. Terribly sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you kindly repeat the question? MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Are there any markings on this piece of paper which would show where this document came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there's not any marking on that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. May I interrupt? I would like for the record to make clear that we are talking of the document marked yesterday with the number 113, and I would request, if possible, the witness be provided with the original of this document. Is that the original? Okay. Thank you. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I had asked for the original. Mr. Moerbauer, is there any mark on this document whereby it can be indicated that you received this document from your colleague, Navrat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no marking on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moerbauer. May I show you now the next document, which you also viewed yesterday, and since the Prosecution is asking that the document you shown, these documents from his file, folder, I would request that it be done that way.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 117.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the document could be placed under the ELMO. Thank you. (Handed to Prosecution). (Handed to witness). MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. Moerbauer, the number on this document is 00473044 is not the number that you entered; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not the number I put on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This number was not on this document at any time while it was in the police station in Vienna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, that number was not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No person put this number on this document in your presence; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document contains no signature; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document was not submitted for graphological analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the part of the Federal Police Department in Vienna, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document has no markings -- this document has no markings making it originate either from the apartment or from the Inda-Bau company in Germany; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document is not marked in such a way that it would be clear from it that you received it from Mr. Navrat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's no such mark.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness please be shown this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 121 is the number. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): This number, 0047109, was not written by you, nor was it written in your presence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document was not submitted to graphological expert analysis, the document or the signature it bears?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this document, too, there is no indication to show where the document comes from; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this document, too, there is no indication confirming that you received this paper from your colleague, Navrat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will the witness be shown the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I object, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's hear your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This witness has answered already several times. He has explained in detail the procedure, by what manner he could determine the source of a particular document. That includes referring to his report, to the great report which was marked 104 yesterday. It is clear that he cannot tell from a document itself the source of a document. Also I would add that no documents were submitted for handwriting analysis. Unnecessary and it should be in our opinion a waste of time to follow with this line of questions and procedure for each one of the documents which were recognised by the witness as having been received by Mr. Navrat yesterday, and which he recognised using his report as an aide-memoire. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Turone, do you know why this line of questioning is being pursued?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is my objection, your Honour. After that I defer to you, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If you do know what line of questioning, then I'll know what to say. Now, Ms. Residovic, let's hear your reaction, so that we know exactly why you're pursuing this line of questioning. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, the witness confirmed in this courtroom that each document he reviewed and analysed had a number. I have shown the witness several documents with no indication recognisable by the witness or any third party. So I can put to the witness a more general question. On all the documents that you saw yesterday and which was submitted to you by the Prosecution, do they carry numbers which were not written by you, nor were they put there in your presence? This will facilitate the job for all of us, I hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What does it actually facilitate, because you are not pursuing any particular thing I see. He is not saying these documents as having been got up by him. He's not doing that. He hasn't owned up that he was handed these documents. Are you not suggesting that he should be telling the truth? MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, the witness said that he had marked all the documents he received, and passed them on to the court and the Prosecution with those markings. So far he has not recognised a single one of those markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Your argument is that he made no markings on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Only on the folders, not on the documents. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I'm showing the witness documents that he looked at yesterday and of which he said in the period from 22nd to 2nd he had marked. However, not one of these documents has any marking which would show that those documents were in the hands of this witness, nor is there an indication on the line of custody through which these documents reached the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If that is the line you are pursuing to discredit him for having ever examined the documents, then you might follow that, pursue it. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. Moerbauer, please, the documents that were shown to you bear numbers that start with 00 and then other numbers, as I have read out to you. Is it true that not one of those numbers was put there by you, nor in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, the stamps, a number, was not put there by me but I did recognise one document with the original sticker that I have put on it. I saw that yesterday on a document. I think it was the number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Now apart from your not putting any of the numbers which have been read out, did you put your own identification marks on those documents, which makes you recognise them whenever you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Talking with the Prosecution attorneys I had learned that there was their own numbered system that when identifying these documents I'd asked that my index be used. On my index I put down what the Prosecutor's office was using, and that number was checked by me to see whether it was consistent with the number I had put on there, and then I checked that with the analysis report. So for me it's quite clear what document is involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think you are going about it in a round about way. Now when you were selecting the documents, counsel is trying to find out whether you put your own marks on them. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Rather, the documents I've shown you and that are before the court at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to my numbers and who removed them, I can't say. It was just on one document that I spotted my original reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please show me that document and that reference?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Now is it your evidence that initially you put marks on them but these marks were subsequently removed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The markings have been removed, that's right. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): So the only document shown to you is the document you've now shown, on which you have recognised your mark; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is one document that caught my eye, because of that sticker with the reference. There may be others, but that was just one I happened to spot, shall we say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, you are claiming that somebody removed the marks you put on the documents. You are claiming that somebody removed the marks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, but in the English translation the original reference number is referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, you didn't find anywhere the documents in English; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: A technical problem, your Honour. The folder was lying on my channel so my channel was switched on to the wrong number. I could not hear the translation into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly repeat the question so that she can translate. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): In the course of the search, as far as you know, nowhere were documents in English found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, there were no documents in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer, in addition to the fact that your marks do not exist on the documents, is it also true that there is no mark on any of the documents shown to you during the hearing showing where that document comes from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The individual documents had, except for this exception -- they did not have any of my references. So none of the documents had my references.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I hope you understood the question. There were no marks on those documents indicating the source of such documents, where they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now when it comes to recognising the individual documents, I used the index, and on the basis of the index I can readily ascertain where the individual documents were seized, and what their contents are. That said, with this exception, none of the other documents bear the references I put on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please give me a precise answer once again to this question? Did you see on any of the documents shown to you the indication Inda-Bau, the apartment of Mr. Zejnil Delalic, his office in Munich, or any other such indication to show where the document comes from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Such information and indications does not appear on the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On any of the documents shown to you yesterday or today was there an indication showing that this was a document received by you from your colleagues, Navrat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only indication is on the form where I can see the reference number I put there. Otherwise the only means of identification is using the index, and that's what I did. I used that index in identifying the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All the documents shown to you yesterday and today are in Serbo-Croatian or Croato-Serbian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And all these documents at this point in time are not in a binder that was in that cardboard box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Moerbauer. Therefore, you have been shown some 40 odd documents from the 1091 that were allegedly taken from the premises of Mr. Delalic's and more than 1700 that were allegedly seized in Munich, and with the exception of one you did not see on any the mark that you yourself placed on it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of my analysis, it's not 1700 documents. It's 12 binders and the individual binders were numbered. The various pages were numbered, as it were. I recognised the documents I was presented with and could say what binder they came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Moerbauer, I should like to ask you to look at a number of documents with the help of the usher. They can also be shown to the Prosecution. I should like to ask you whether, among these documents, you recognise documents which could perhaps belong to Mr. Delalic, which were seized in Inda-Bau or in Mr. Delalic's apartment, or which do not belong to those premises at all. The documents are simply being shown as a means of refreshing the witness' memory and not for any other purpose. They are not in evidence at all. They have not been offered. (Handed to Prosecution).

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May we ask -- kindly ask the defence lawyers to explain where do these papers come from and which is the reason for which she wants to show these documents to the witness in case they should be part of the 191 documents she's been talking about. We think that anyway the witness should be given time to consult his papers, his files, because no policeman at all could on the spot immediately recognise every single other document which was not dealt with as relevant in this case in these very days. Thank you. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): The witness has testified under oath that he put his mark on any document he looked at. So I'm asking the witness to look at these five documents to see whether there are any marks, and four out of those five documents was received by the defence from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Anyway, as I said already, if these documents are described in the report, the witness has to be given the possibility to consult the report. Otherwise if they're not in the report he has to be allowed to go back to Vienna and consult all the possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly show the document to the witness. Let him know whether he could ... MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Just asking the witness to say whether on any one of these documents there is a mark that he put on them and by which he can recognise the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to any marking I might have put there, there isn't any such. This document is one I do not remember. Using my index, I could ascertain with regard to these documents -- I could tell you how they are referred to and what binders they were in. So if you would give me leave to do that ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. It's not necessary. Simply on any -- you did not recognise your mark on any one of these documents. Thank you. I have finished my cross-examination. You can give me back those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I ask the document to be marked for identification anyway. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): These documents were given to the witness just to remind him and there is no need for them to be identified.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is an Act in the procedure. The witness is being shown documents. This is a document. This is not evidence, but the Registry has to keep a copy of those documents:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise. We will come back at 12 o'clock. (11.35 am) (Short break)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honours please, may I raise a point on behalf of the prosecution arising out of the cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We may wait for the witness to return, or I can make my submission in the absence of the witness. It doesn't matter. Your Honours, having heard the cross-examination of this witness and of the fact that there has been a whole series of documents that have been put to the witness in the course of that cross-examination, and having regard to what happened when the documents were presented to the witness in the terms of the purpose for which they are given, we call upon Madam Residovic to tender the documents in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You think she should tender it even if she does not want to?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Even if she doesn't want to, your Honour, we call on her to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Perhaps my learned friend might tell us why he says they should do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Certainly, your Honours. I will be happy to do that. Your Honours, the documents were put to the witness for a number of reasons. They fall basically into three main categories. The first category is that the documents that were shown and what the witness responded to in relation to them, in our submission proves that this witness can identify the documents. Having regard to the nature of his evidence and the purpose of his evidence, it's in our submission very important that we see the documents that he was able to identify. So we're not submitting that the documents should go to your Honours as proof of their contents. We are not suggesting that at all at this stage. We may assert at a later stage that your Honours should accept them for the truth of their contents. What we're saying, though, is that having regard to the cross-examination these documents, when put to the witness, were spoken of by him in a way which goes to show that he was familiar with them and was capable of dealing with them. Now certainly there are exceptions, as Judge Jan had pointed out, that he cannot talk about whether he knew the handwriting of a witness. He can't talk about whether he knew where precisely they came from, but he was able to give some evidence of the provenance of these documents and his ability to identify them. We submit that that is relevant and it's properly admissible and, of course, without the documents themselves the evidence is incomplete. Another basis, your Honour, is that we submit that with the -- my German is not so good -- the Niederschrift document, which I think is the records which were shown to the witness, and the search warrant itself, this is evidence that there was regularity in the procedures that were followed, and that the police in Vienna had gone according to law in the methods about which they sought to seize these documents. Now there may be arguments that the letter of the law was not complied with in every particular aspect, but it is certainly evidence of the fact that procedures were followed according to law. We submit when it comes to the tendering of the documents, this is relevant. It's for these reasons we believe that even if it's out of the mouth of the defence, it's still relevant and should be tendered. If the defence decline to tender them, as I've called for them to be tendered, then in my submission the Prosecution seeks for them to be tendered at this stage. Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, first, my learned friend seems to forget they have already introduced the search warrant into evidence. I believe it is Prosecution 102, 103, somewhere around in there. Secondly, these documents have all been marked as Prosecution Exhibits. It's the Prosecution's job to show their admissibility, and so far all they've proven is that officer Moerbauer examined them at some point in history. They haven't shown where these things came from, that they're authentic, anything. All they have shown is Moerbauer saw them in his office in Vienna and that they'd arrived there through various permutations. That doesn't get them there, your Honour. They still aren't there for admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If my understanding is correct, that's not the issue at this stage. He's only trying to show that there was a system adopted by Moerbauer in determining what documents he would admit or do things which he included in those files. That is all he's trying to show to avoid the general argument that he never knew what documents were there or not. Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Somehow things seem to have gotten confused, your Honour. I think what my colleague from the Prosecution was talking about were the last three or four documents that Ms. Residovic had the witness take a look at to see if he could identify them. What the Prosecution seems to be asking is that they be made a part of the record in the case. My understanding was that the Registrar announced that they would be made a part of the record in the case and a copy would be made for the record in the case, and that should end the matter. If what the Office of the Prosecutor is asking is that they further be admitted in evidence, I think that's improper, because they were used strictly for impeachment purposes and not for the contents of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: They can be marked for the purpose of identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think that's what has been done. So I think from that standpoint it has been taken care of.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might I respond, your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Before you carry on, is my definition of your position correct, that you are merely using it to test whether Moerbauer had a system for identifying those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Exactly, your Honour. When showing the documents -- while he was able to do that, we submit they should be tendered on that basis, not merely marked for identification, because of his proof of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Already his evidence to that was the answer to the document which was shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, but in my submission the evidence is not complete without the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: The documents have been accepted as the documents shown to him, which he acknowledged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But is it part of the evidence, your Honour? I mean, it's one thing to mark something for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: No, not strictly part of the evidence but he has identified those documents shown to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In our submission, your Honour, that is a proper basis for admissibility. If the witness is shown a document -- now, it's not correct to say that he was impeached on the documents. It may certainly have been counsel's intention to impeach. (a) We say that didn't succeed at all and (b) we say that something else happened in the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose that is the result of your new argument, that the impeachment wasn't successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Because of what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Counsel deliberately and intentionally led the witness on into other areas. If counsel had not intended that, that is regrettable but counsel did it. That is on the record. We submit the record is now incomplete, because the witness has testified as to certain documents, which are not in evidence. We submit that they should be put into evidence, and we request that that happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: My apprehension mainly is there was no evidence laid for the foundation of admitting those papers other than showing him those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I understand that, your Honour. That may be a problem if we were trying to rely on them for the truth of their contents but I make it clear that they are not at this stage. We are merely trying to rely on the documents to show that these are the particular documents that the witness was shown and from which he was able to demonstrate to your Honours that there was a system in place and he was familiar with that system and he knew how to use it. In our submission, at this stage that's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We have yet to determine from which they were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Of course, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: So when this is done, then perhaps all your folders, whatever they are, they will become part of the record then. The probative value of this document can be taken up at a later stage. Let us first of all find out from what source they came.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If I may, your Honour, certainly that is something we have undertaken to do and we will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mark them for identification purposes at this stage. This document was shown. Now what this document is, from where it came is yet to be established by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Certainly, you were, but if I may press the point, the point is that we're not seeking to tender them for the truth of their contents, which would obviously be very important to establish that chain at this stage if we sought to tender them, but we're not doing that. All we are seeking to do at this stage is part of the system of identification. Now it may be, your Honours, that some of the documents or all of the documents may not ultimately be admitted, but it may still be a very relevant issue to the proceedings as to whether there is an appropriate system in place and through that system certain of the documents could be identified and whether or not there are procedures that were followed according to law. In our submission, these documents would prove that and that alone, and should, therefore, at this stage be admitted. I accept, your Honour, that with change --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down a little bit for the interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Actually it was a matter of convenience that we examine Mr. Moerbauer at this stage otherwise the persons who discovered the documents should have come first and then he could have said: "These are the documents I examined and these are the contents of the documents" and his report comes in. If that would have happened in the proper course, first examine Mr. Navrat, examine Mr. Unger, then this gentleman come: "Yes, I received these documents from them and this is what I found in them". As a matter of convenience we allowed Mr. Moerbauer to be examined first. The defence would never get any opportunity after that to show this document to this witness. Therefore we are making them at this stage only for the purpose of identification. Let Mr. Navrat come. Let Mr. Unger come. Since these are the documents we located from the premises occupied or in the possession of the accused -- normally actually the person who recovered the documents from the spot would have come first but as a matter of convenience we allowed this gentleman to give his evidence at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Having regard to the rules of the Tribunal in relation to evidence, it would have been entirely possible to present all of the documents without calling a witness at all. Now that may have caused difficulties in relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You see, under Rule 95 the defence has a right to say these documents were not properly taken into custody. If they can establish that, the documents will probably be not admitted into evidence. At this stage how can we say: let them be admitted into evidence. All we are doing at this stage is allowing these documents to be marked for the purpose of identification and this has been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But it is a question of weight, your Honour. If the documents are admitted into evidence and the Prosecution has not adequately, properly or otherwise established the province of them, it may be that your Honours choose to either reject them from evidence or, alternatively, you say: "We give them no weight" but in proceedings that have happened before this Tribunal on previous occasions this sort of objection has been taken and certainly witnesses have been called, but not necessarily always the case, because your Honours are not a jury; you are judges. You have the ability, the skill and the training to be able to remove things from your mind and not take them into consideration if they are admitted and you choose later not to accept them. Now, in my submission, imposing the traditional jury type rules and regulations of evidence in relation to these proceedings will do nothing except extend them for a very, very long period of time, when your Honours are perfectly capable and skilful enough and trained to be able to do all of that with documents that are admitted into evidence and which you later choose to apply no weight to. My submission, and I'm getting away from my original submission to your Honours, but I do submit that on the basis that I have raised that these documents should be admitted. They should be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Niemann, I agree with you that you need supporting evidence for whatever testimony he gave before the Trial Chamber, but I think it's sufficient for us to look at it. The discredit of the witness wasn't complete, because he actually established that he had the system by which he determined how the documents were brought and that is the result of cross-examination. So I regard it as unnecessary to get in the documents which will show nothing more than the fact that you rely on those documents for showing that he recognised the system he used in determining the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just very briefly, I think there may be a simple solution. If the Registrar would advise Mr. Niemann of the numbers he has assigned to these documents, then he will know what numbers have been assigned to them. Secondly, I think there's some misapprehension about the record. What Mr. Moerbauer said was given time, he believed he would be able to identify these. He did not actually go to his papers and say: "This particular document came from this particular case". So the record should be clear about that. All he said was he believed he might be able to do that or could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Actually Mr. Niemann was not talking only of the three documents shown to the witness at the end. He was referring to documents shown also earlier to the witness, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we have the witness? (Witness re-enters court) (Interpreter re-enters court)

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, given the lack of earphones up here, I think we're going to have to take a couple of minutes to situate ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: May it please the court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Moerbauer. My name is Tom Moran and I represent a gentleman here named Hazim Delic. I'm going to ask you a few questions about your training and experience and a few questions about what occurred in here in your direct examination. If you have any questions about what I ask you, will you stop me and we'll clarify it? One other thing, there's a lady sitting right up there named Melanie. She's the court reporter. Melanie has to take down every word that we say in here and she can't take down a nod.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've understood you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, officer. By the way, you've testified before, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has already answered that question earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. As I recall your testimony earlier today -- earlier during your testimony you testified that from 1981-1984 you were in a basic police school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And during that three year course of instruction did you get any instruction on handling of physical evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And, in fact, I'll bet that during your instruction in physical evidence they told you that it was very important that when evidence was seized, it should be accounted for properly at the time it was seized, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When objects are seized, you have to be able to say where they were seized from. It doesn't say exactly how you go about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, but what I'm getting at is your training taught you to be careful about accounting for evidence that was seized, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And then you had four years of experience as a police officer in Vienna. Was that what we would call in my country a street cop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I served in the First District of Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: As what we would call a patrol officer, someone wearing a uniform driving around in a marked car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was a patrol officer with a uniform and I did patrol in a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: During that four years as a patrol officer did you have any occasion to seize evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did have such occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And I'll bet on each and every occasion you made sure that the evidence that you said you seized was what you actually seized, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The difference between the duty at the time was that objects were seized that were on a different basis, that is to say I did not seize objects on the basis of a court warrant at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Now the question I asked was: when you seized evidence while you were a patrol officer in Vienna from 1984-1988, did you account for that evidence that you seized? Stated a little bit differently, did you make sure that what you turned in was what you had seized?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now that brings us to 1988. I understand between 1991 and 1992 you were in a two year detective course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was a detective Kriminalbeamter course. It lasts for one year. As far as I can remember from October 1992 -- no, that course of instruction lasted from October 1991-October 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: During that course you were trained to be a detective?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The course lasts for a year and is four months on hands training in a police station in a detective unit, and the other eight months consists of theoretical instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Inspector, I'll bet during either that hands-on training or during the classroom training, somebody talked about the proper handling of evidence, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: By the way, when I say hands-on training, I mean the practical training where you were assigned to a detective unit. I'll bet that that training included properly inventorying what you seized and properly accounting for it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to seized objects, the stickers are put on them so that it can be ascertained where they were seized. Now whether this concerns the items in bulk or individual items, that is not specified as a rule. It is settled on a case-by-case basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well, let me give you an example. Suppose that you filled out a form that said you'd seized 30 kg of cocaine or 30 packages of $20 bills each containing $1,000. Later when that cocaine or packages of $20 bills were counted, there were only 28. Would there just be a correction made to the report, or would somebody run an investigation on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you have a suitcase that's seized and it contains cocaine or money, then you can describe it. I can put a note on it: "Contents: 1 kilo of cocaine and so-and-so many dollars" or I can put a slip on it -- I can put a slip on the suitcase, on the cocaine and on the money, and then it doesn't really matter what the exact amount is. A note goes into the record and then one has to determine whether there's been some inappropriate behaviour. One has to ascertain what became of the cocaine or the money.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So what I'm getting at is if you thought that you'd seized 30 kilos of cocaine, you would put down some place that you'd seized 30 kilos of cocaine, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If later there turned out only to be 28 kilos of cocaine somebody would ask some questions, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Why are videotapes any different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to the videotapes, a note was entered into the record about the number and that was passed on to the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So somebody, when they seized a bunch of videotapes, wrote down that they had seized 30 and, in fact, only had seized 28. That's no big deal; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Vienna District Court was informed of the situation, and should they have assumed there was some inappropriate behaviour or theft, then that would have been considered to be an offence and legal action would have been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Let's flip it to the other side, detective. How about if you said you'd seized 51 kilograms of cocaine and later on it turned out you said you had 54? Would anybody ask any questions about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At all events a record would be made of the state of affairs and the court would be informed thereof. That's what happened with the videotapes. The court was informed thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: What I am getting at, detective, is would you be more careful if you were doing cocaine rather than videotapes? Videotapes aren't that important; is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The videotapes were secured as evidence and it doesn't matter whether videotape or cocaine is involved. I, at all events, would handle these objects exactly like cocaine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That's right. The way you'd handle cocaine or videotapes would be someone would seize it, someone would inventory it, be it 51 kilograms of cocaine or 51 videotapes. Someone would count it, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And you'd expect the count to be right, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, with regard to the number of the videotapes that was subsequently corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and what I'm getting at is you would expect the count on the scene, when it was seized, to be accurate, wouldn't you? I mean, it's not hard for a trained police officer to count from 1-51, is it, or from 1-54?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally only seized four videos and there were four videos. Now with regard to the other video tapes, you'll have to ask my colleagues who seized them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: All right. It's not hard for a trained police officer to count from 1-51, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He is challenging the ability of the Austrian police to make correct counts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well, your Honour, either a trained police officer can count from 1-51 or he can't. Either he can be expected to count from 1-51 and do it right or he can't. This man is much more experienced in the Austrian police than I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The basis of my objection, your Honour, is what is the relevance of whether Austrian police can count from 1-51 or 1-100. It is absurd to be putting these questions to this witness. Counsel knows the answer clearly and everybody else in this courtroom knows the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You have got the answer from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason that question was asked is somebody counted 51 video tapes. Now there are three extras. We have no idea where these three extras came from. We ought to be able to presume that the officer who seized them seized them correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Actually there have been three counting errors. One of 30 to 28. Then the total in the report is shown at 83, whereas it should be 86.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: On that last one, my maths being what it is, I'll give him that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Go straight into your object of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Detective, you testified yesterday you watched 60 video cassettes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: By my maths about 82 were seized; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 86, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. You testified this morning that you watched things that were taken off the air and you watched comedy shows and you watched folk singing. What's on those other 20 some odd tapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about 20 or more videos which I did not see. Now, as to precisely which ones I saw and which I didn't see, I can't answer that, but at all events an index was drawn up in relation to the videotapes and there you can find the contents of the said videotapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Could the Registrar please show this man Prosecution Exhibit 139? Detective, I'm going to have shown to you something that has been marked for identification as Prosecution Exhibit 139. (Handed to witness). Now, detective, that's something that purports to be a judgment from a court, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Do you or any member, to your knowledge, of the Austrian police have the slightest idea of whether or not that is a true and correct copy of the original judgment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to this document, it was not checked to see whether it was genuine, but via a note in the record the competent judge was informed of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And the competent judge is Judge Seda; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Seda or Dr. Bornath.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Are either one of them the judges that entered that judgment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, neither of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: In fact, that judgment didn't even come from an Austrian court, did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: In fact, I could have sat down at my typewriter and typed that thing, if I spoke Serbo-Croatian. You wouldn't know, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That possibility would exist, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the search warrant in this case? If not, we can find a copy of it for you in German, I believe. Are you familiar with the search warrant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with it to an extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: It authorised you to seize documents about war crimes in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in particular video recordings about the torture of prisoners; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Would you like to see a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: It's in the record. It was introduced by the Prosecution. I believe it's Prosecution Exhibit 101, 102 or 103. MS van DUSSCHOTEN: It's D29/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I thought that Mr. Turone introduced it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO BENITO
utterances.text: May I remind you of the difficulties of the interpreters. You speak terribly fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I'll try and slow down. I try. Sometimes I don't succeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO BENITO
utterances.text: You forget it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sometimes I don't succeed. In fact, often I don't succeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO BENITO
utterances.text: Normally you don't succeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The train of thought is too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Detective, could you read on the back what the Exhibit Number is? There is an Exhibit Number on the back. Just flip it over, so the record is clear what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: IT-96-21-T, Exhibit Number D29/1, Trial Chamber 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That's a true and correct copy of the search want; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I believe yesterday you testified that having watched all those videotapes, that there was -- that having watched about 60 videotapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That the only thing that you saw that looked like a war crime or looked like torture was "one person, a prisoner no doubt, had to do push-ups".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Detective, have you ever been in the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I wasn't in the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's too young.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: At police school perhaps did they have a thing called physical training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I'll bet there was someone when you were taking physical training at the police school who was very much like my drill sergeant when I was in basic training. He was known to say: "Moran, drop and give me 25".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not refer to the push-ups yesterday as mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: No. As I recall, what you said was that was the only possible mistreatment that you saw in the videotapes; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact words I used. I said that somebody was obliged to do push-ups. As to whether that was mistreatment or not or whether I said that, but I do not record push-ups as mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So if push-ups aren't mistreatment, having watched 60 videotapes, you didn't see any mistreatment at all; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now, as I see mistreatment, I did not see anything resembling mistreatment, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So you didn't find any recordings about the torture of prisoners, video recordings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see any tortures or mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Also a couple of days ago you testified about Sanda Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And one of the things you said was -- you were being asked whether she was an adult or not, and you noted that she was over 14 and said, according to the transcript: "She was not a child according to our legal system".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So that a 14 year old child can marry without permission under your legal system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
